scope: Bounded rule analysis, incremental parsing, optional SDK background writes

failure_checks: Real trickling HTTP response interrupted; same step recovered as a report revision
Blocked FIFO history read interrupted without worker artifact writes
SIGTERM of CLI reaped its worker
Split UTF-8, append, truncate, atomic replace, larger rewrite, delete and cache capacity fallback
Slow SDK storage, queue record/byte saturation, coalescing, disk write error and bounded close
Concurrent span writes and fork while parent lock held; no duplicated parent event

cache_measurement.scope: local JSONL parse/query cost, each file measured separately
limitations: No network queries or full diagnosis latency measured
Cache still iterates retained records; this is not an indexed time-window lookup
Overflow uses full scans; memory budgets are shared across cached files in an engine

real_verl.diagnostic_backend: deliberately unreachable loopback endpoint; missing evidence retained

documentation: Strict Sphinx build, compileall and tracked shell syntax passed
limits: Deadlines apply separately to scheduling and each interval analysis, not to a whole batch or run
Process cleanup adds at most 0.5 seconds of configured waits; kernel uninterruptible I/O and OS scheduling cannot be guaranteed to finish immediately
Parent report persistence remains synchronous and should use local storage
JSONL cache requires append-only newline-terminated records or atomic replacement; arbitrary in-place middle edits are unsupported
Cache limits bound retained decoded record count and source bytes, not exact Python heap usage; overflow preserves results by full scan
Cache avoids repeated JSON parsing but still filters records; no persistent time-window index
SDK JSON serialization remains on the caller; async I/O may drop records and in-flight writes can finish after bounded close
Real VERL test was a small one-host integration fixture with unreachable monitoring backend; no throughput or physical multi-node claim
